sentences.text:
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 1
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.345 Of 2015
Judgment:
(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili)
Aggrieved by the order dated 13.08.2012 passed in L.A.O.P.No.93 of 2002 by the I Additional District Judge, Nizamabad, the present appeal has been filed.

2. Heard learned Government Pleader for Acquisition appearing for the appellant.
3. It is the case of the appellant that they have acquired the lands of the respondents in an extent of Ac.2.21 guntas by issuing notification dated 22.06.1996 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act'), and possession was taken on 24.08.1996.
The Land Acquisition Officer has passed Award on 15.12.1997 fixing compensation of Rs.28,200/- per acre.

The respondents have sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the said reference was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.93 of 2002, and the Reference Court has enhanced the compensation from Rs.28,000/- to that of Rs.1,46,750/- per acre vide order dated 13.08.2012.

4. Learned Government Pleader had contended that no reasons were assigned by the Reference Court as to why the compensation was enhanced to nearly seven times than what was awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

Learned Government Pleader had further contended that since no reasons were assigned by the Reference Court, appropriate orders be passed in the present appeal by setting aside the order passed by the Reference Court.

5. In view of the said submissions, this Court is of the considered view that the Reference Court has enhanced the compensation based upon the registered sale deed bearing No.918 of 1993, dated 30.08.1993 and also the order dated 24.10.2005 passed in O.P.No.95 of 1999 by the I Additional District Court, Nizamabad and also the common judgment dated 01.12.2004 passed by this Court in A.S.No.2661 of 2003 and 668 of 2004.

Further, a perusal of the order passed by the Reference Court The Revenue Divisional Officer vs Yerra Narayana And 13 Others on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103407268/
1 at paragraph No.14

entities.text: Reference Court The Revenue Divisional Officer vs Yerra Narayana And 13 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: discloses that the appellant has not raised any objection while fixing the market value of the land acquired and accepted the sale under Ex.A1.
When once the appellant has accepted the market value, the Reference Court was justified in enhancing the compensation from Rs.28,200/- to Rs.1,46,750/-.
Even otherwise, the extent of land acquired from the respondents is Ac.2.21 guntas.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the Reference Court.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

___________________________________ JUSTICE ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI ________________________________________ JUSTICE LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY Date: 07.08.2024 rkk The Revenue Divisional Officer vs Yerra Narayana And 13 Others on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103407268/
